frame: metres; X forward, Y left, Z up; floor z=0; zero pose standing, arms down, palms in

actuators._about: Off-the-shelf actuators we can buy (RobStride QDD modules). Peak torque, no-load speed (+-10 %), mass and gear from RobStride's Product_Information spec table of 2026-07-13 (github.com/RobStride/Product_Information). rated_nm from each module's manual (section 1.2), where it differs from that table: RS03 20 not 21, RS02 6 not 7. Sizes from the maker's STEP files of 2026-10-30, read as edges and circles and checked against their CIRCLE radii: 'h' the length along the output including the hub, 'r' the half of the largest round envelope, ears and connector bump included, 'depth' the fore-aft size with the ears turned to their best (RS03, RS06) in a limb where only one direction is tight. The motors stay simple cylinders: r where they turn or sit in the open, depth / 2 where the ears are turned (the ankle). 'rating_note' gives the plate each rating needs, and the stall figures, which are one reader's reading of each manual's second overload chart: confirm on the bench. 'ratio' > 1 means an extra linkage reduction after the module (torque x ratio, speed / ratio). Joint dynamics (tools/make_robot_files.py; 2026-10-31 ESTIMATES: RobStride publishes no rotor inertia in its spec tables; K-Bot's MJCF uses 0.005 / 0.0015 / 0.005 / 0.007 kg m2 armature on RS00 / 02 / 03 / 04, tuned values up to 5 x from ours): 'gear' the module's reduction, 'rotor_kgm2' the motor rotor's inertia, scaled from the frame size against Unitree's 7520 motor (5e-5 kg m2, from G1's armature 0.0102 at 14.3:1); reflected at the output as armature = rotor x gear^2; 'damping_nms' viscous and 'friction_nm' Coulomb friction at the output, typical of QDD modules (friction about 2-3 % of peak torque).

RS02.rating_note: 6 N m on a 260 x 280 mm plate (manual); 7 in its overload table

RS03.rating_note: 20 N m on a 215 x 220 mm plate (manual); about 13 at stall. T-N curve ends at 188 rpm under load

RS06.rating_note: 11 N m on a 130 x 160 mm plate (manual); about 8 at stall. T-N curve ends at 430 rpm under load

RS04.rating_note: 40 N m on 345 x 345 mm, 35 on 220 x 200 mm (spec table, at 50 rpm); about 28.5 at stall. T-N curve ends at 190 rpm under load

knit_pa12.note: PA12 (MJF) cover under a knit sleeve: 1010 kg/m3 plus 0.3 kg/m2 of knit over a 3 mm wall

pc.note: polycarbonate: the glossy black covers; the visor is a 2 mm layer

al7075.note: 7075-T6 frames, brackets, flanges, cranks and rods, with a fill factor

electronics.note: compute, power board, cameras: explicit masses

garment.note: the grey skin, per m2 as the 3 mm PA12 and knit cover it replaced (3.3 kg/m2): knit about 0.5, foam about 0.3, and about 2.5 held for the inner frames, which are not designed. An estimate carried over so the masses do not fall on a guess

hand.note: the hand's motors, tendons and palm: explicit mass

steel.note: screws, pins and bearings: role hardware or bearing, explicit mass from spec/hardware.py (catalogue, or geometry times density)

brass.note: heat-set inserts: explicit mass from spec/hardware.py

build.why: the flange on the hip yaw's hub, on the hip, before the leg comes up
the motor into the barrel from the open end, hub first; 10 M4 from the inboard side, nothing there yet
the cap, skirt to the motor's back, post out; 6 flush M3

fork and cup, bearing and nut on the cup, ring loose behind them, from inboard: the slot passes over the barrel, the cup into the bore. 9 M5 through the eye; the ring turned through the opening with a pin spanner
the outer cheek, bearing and ring in it, from outboard onto the post. 4 M5 into the crown, then the washer
the hubs last: 2 M4 each, a key through the hole under the mark
the ankle motors and rods are in from behind by now (their own round); the panel closes the section with 7 flush M3
the leg up to the flange: 6 M4 from below, up beside the tube

assumptions.source: RS02 User Manual 260713 section 1.1: 6-M4 7 MIN. User's choice, 2026-11-05
assumptions.risk: Not used yet: no RS02 hub is bolted in the spec

assumptions.source: User's rule, 2026-11-05: no load on rear threads that are not on a drawing. RS04's rear 10-M4 is on its drawing; RS03 and RS06 rear ears and RS02's through-holes are not
assumptions.risk: RS04's rear 10-M4 is drawn but its rated use isn't stated

assumptions.source: User's rule, 2026-11-05. Proof and breaking loads: ISO 898-1 via hardware_catalog.json (wuerth p3)
assumptions.risk: RobStride gives no grade or torque. A softer hub thread may need less

assumptions.source: Usual target for reusable joints (Shigley, VDI 2230 practice)
assumptions.risk: Scatter in tightening is about +-25 % with a torque wrench: separation margins carry it

assumptions.source: Black-oxide steel screw, dry or lightly oiled (Shigley)
assumptions.risk: Sets the torque quoted, not the capacities

assumptions.source: Bare aluminium on aluminium for slip, as tools/strength.py BOLT_SLIP_N already used
assumptions.risk: Anodised or oiled faces can be lower: slip margins scale with it directly

assumptions.unit: share of external tension the screw sees
assumptions.source: Typical screw in short metal clamp (VDI 2230 range about 0.1 to 0.3)
assumptions.risk: Small: tension margins are mostly preload

assumptions.source: 6061-T6 shear strength (ASM). RobStride's housing and hub alloys are unknown
assumptions.risk: A casting (ADC12 about 185 MPa, estimate) drops the strip margin by a tenth

assumptions.source: 7075-T6 shear strength (ASM)
assumptions.risk: Only for threads tapped in our own parts

assumptions.source: Same factor as tools/strength.py SF_MIN. The stripping area is the standard one for an internal thread (ISO 898 / FED-STD-H28), which assumes even load across the threads; first threads carry more
assumptions.risk: The check limits preload by this; it does not model fatigue of the thread
assumptions.settled_by: Bossard calculator for the alloy, or a pull test

assumptions.source: hardware_catalog.json thread_engagement.aluminium (project rule, top of Bossard F.044's range)
assumptions.risk: RobStride's threads are shallower than this by drawing: see the 'fastener' group

assumptions.source: Twice ISO 2768-m's +-0.1 mm for parts this size: the least running gap that is still a gap once made
assumptions.risk: Stack of three parts can use it up

assumptions.source: IKO CAT-57166 p8: on Super Slim, 'fit based on the actual measured dimensions' and 'a slight interference fit'. Seats are drawn at nominal diameter
assumptions.risk: Interference eats internal clearance at 70 to 90 %: machined to the bearing in hand

assumptions.value: 2 bearings, lever rule; the motor's own bearing takes none
assumptions.source: RobStride publishes no output bearing rating, so nothing is rested on it (reports/actuator_interfaces.md). Real share goes by stiffness: the motor's bearing will take some, which helps the two supports and loads it unrated
assumptions.risk: HIGH: knee capacities assume the fork shares load between the two supports only, with no flex in 3 mm cheeks
assumptions.settled_by: RobStride question 2; FEA of the fork

assumptions.value: the ankle motor's rated torque limits the lever
assumptions.source: A load repeated every step can only be held by what a motor sustains: RS06 rated 11 N m x 1.32 linkage, so 18 mm at 810 N. Static cases keep the peak
assumptions.risk: A faster walk or jog passes 810 N (reports/strength.md: to 2,220 N)

assumptions.source: IKO CAT-57166 Table 5: 1.2 to 1.5 normal operation, 1.5 to 3 with shock. Walking taken at the boundary
assumptions.risk: Shock loads would use a higher factor

assumptions.source: IKO CAT-57166 Table 4: 1.5 or more for normal operation
assumptions.risk: A fall isn't in the load cases at all

assumptions.source: 8 h a day x 1 cycle a second x 365 days x 3 years: a hand figure for a service life, no product requirement behind it
assumptions.risk: A real duty cycle may be half or twice this

assumptions.source: Knee swing in a calm walk (human about 60 deg). Not measured on echo's take
assumptions.risk: Enters the oscillating-life formula as a straight factor

assumptions.source: Iteration 41: the garment's density held 2.5 kg/m2 of undesigned formers. The shank's closed body now fills that skin to 3 mm, and the thigh needs only ribs off its tube. Knit 0.5 and foam 0.3 kg/m2 are the note in spec/robot.py MATERIALS
assumptions.risk: Up to 1.0 kg on the robot if formers are heavier than this. Nothing here is weighed
assumptions.settled_by: Design the thigh's ribs; a coupon of the knit and foam

assumptions.value: threaded rings M68 x 1, nut M50 x 1
assumptions.source: Thin rings, made not bought. Thread forms aren't drawn: the rings and nut are plain bands in the spec. Tightened with a pin spanner, locked with thread adhesive
assumptions.risk: Race axial load on a fine thread in 7075: not calculated; a circlip needs 2.65 mm of groove and 4 mm more width each side, estimate
assumptions.settled_by: FEA of the collar; a trial fit

assumptions.value: paste in the bore, gap pad on the skirt
assumptions.source: reports/strength.md counts these as contact area. No resistance is modelled, and the bore's 0.05 mm gap is a nominal
assumptions.risk: Rated torque isn't transferred from the maker's plate

assumptions.source: Steel, for screw masses: geometry times density, as no maker's mass table was read
assumptions.risk: None that matters
